narrative.overview:
The North Star is carried as tuned, warm, human precision: instruments calibrated by hand until they read true. Its literal CRT reading — the amber-on-black HUD workspace this world replaced — is still refused as a *look*: no monochrome amber field, no glowing terminal furniture, no amber on everything. The amber itself was never the rut, and it returns on purpose: the brand's own LX-plate yellow is the map's one action colour, a single lit plate on a cold slate field. The world that expresses it is the Trail Map: the tracker reads as one surveyed mountain at two times of day. The default is the floodlit night map, a cold slate field with lit ribbons and crisp signage plates; the switch gives the printed day map, the night slate lifted to daylight — cool survey stock with the same ribbons and the same plates. The day map is a translation of the same mountain, never an inversion.

The world lends type, palette, density, and one signature move. It never supplies layout, navigation model, or controls: nav is nav, buttons are buttons, tables sort with standard headers. A working screen must read as a tracker of its category first. The voice is warm, playful, and tactile, and it lives in the display layers only. Every control and state keeps its plain name (New task, Blocked, Needs attention); metaphor display names sit beside plain truth (Trail profile, with the plain sub-line Milestones and sprint progress). The ornament budget is spent entirely in the signature panel; lists and forms stay bare.

Density is the working loop. The dashboard holds six regions inside a 1440x900 viewport at trail-report density, lists run at 36px rows on desktop and 44px on touch, and every count is a tabular figure. Panels sit flat on the ground; only overlays lift. Motion is a surveyed redraw, never ambient: lines draw once per mount and stop.
keyCharacteristics: One mountain, two times of day: floodlit night map by default, printed day map on switch, same furniture in both.
Three type voices with strict jobs: Signage caps for plates and labels, Guide for all readable copy, Surveyor tabular figures for every number.
Difficulty ribbons encode priority and nothing else, always doubled by their rank numeral and the configured priority name.

Brand amber is the only action colour: primary buttons, focus ring, today marker, and the "You are here" post; at day the hue splits at the paper line into the plate-yellow fill and the ink-amber marks and links.
Trail-report density: 36px desktop rows, 44px touch rows, 4px spacing scale, whole-cell repack.
Hybrid elevation: flat bordered panels everywhere, one shadow layer reserved for lifted overlays.
Motion draws once (180 to 260ms linear) and snaps to final state under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Plain-Name Rule
rules.body: Metaphor display names never replace a plain truth. Every region head carries a plain sub-line (Trail profile reads Milestones and sprint progress), role keycaps always carry the real role in the accessible label, and every button names its action literally.

rules.name: The Job-Colour Rule
rules.body: Ribbon colour encodes priority; series hues encode identity; state hues encode meaning. A colour never holds two jobs on one screen, and no colour appears decoratively.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every difficulty ribbon carries its rank numeral on the chip and the project's configured priority name in its accessible label. Colour is the fast path, never the only path.

rules.name: The Same-Mountain Rule
rules.body: The day map is a translation, never an inversion. Ribbons keep their fills, plates keep their anatomy, and only paper, ink, and rim change with the light.

rules.name: The Snow-Ink Rule
rules.body: Body ink is snow-white at night (#EAF2F6 register), never pure #FFFFFF, and never a light-mode inversion of the same value. Ink always comes from the map's own palette.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Signage names things in caps plates, Guide reads as sentences, Surveyor reports figures. There is no fourth voice and no family outside these three.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every count, key, date, and time is set with tabular figures so numbers align from row to row and column to column. A proportional figure in a count is a defect.

rules.name: The Whole-Cell Repack Rule
rules.body: Every cap and grid repacks in whole cells. A scroller is capped to whole rows measured from the rendered row height (the movement strip reads its cap from the DOM, so it lands on three 40px rows or five 30px rows, never a half row), and a card is never cut.

rules.name: The Guide-Word Rule
rules.body: Every panel head names the span in view. The Trail Profile sub-line reads Milestones and sprint progress, followed by the live date span (Sep 27 to Nov 21), and it recomputes as content passes.

rules.name: The Side-Fill Discipline Rule
rules.body: Capacity and WIP fills are exactly proportional to real counts against the ruled limit. The limit is ruled at the meter's end as a 2px line, the fill never overshoots it, and the meter never lies by scale.

rules.name: The Duration-as-Length Rule
rules.body: Every time bar is exactly proportional to real duration. Sprint runs descend at their true span; where truth to scale fails (a run without dates), ticks and numerals replace the decorative bar, and a minimum length is used only when there is nothing to measure.

rules.name: The One-Lift Rule
rules.body: Exactly one shadow vocabulary is reserved for lifted overlays (dialogs, slideovers, popovers, dragging cards). Nothing else floats: not rows, not plates, not panels, not buttons at rest.

rules.name: The Route Trace Rule
rules.body: The signature interaction is hover-or-focus driven, keyboard equivalent, cleared by blur or Escape, and additive: it draws the route and leaves every standard control (click to open the slideover) untouched.

rules.name: The State-Is-Signal Rule
rules.body: Colour, position, and motion communicate priority, type, WIP state, and sync state. A surface that renders state ambiguously is a defect, and a decorative use of a state colour is the same defect in reverse.

rules.name: The Surveyed-Redraw Rule
rules.body: Motion is a redraw of surveyed lines, once per mount: 180ms for the Route Trace, 220ms for the profile runs, both linear, both inside the 180 to 260ms band. Nothing loops, breathes, or eases in ambiently except the loading skeleton pulse, and reduced motion snaps every draw to its final state.

dos: Do keep every colour on its job: ribbon for priority, series hue for identity, state hue for meaning, brand amber for action and position.
Do double every ribbon with its rank numeral on the chip and the project's configured priority name in the accessible label.
Do set every count, key, date, and time in the Surveyor voice with tabular figures.
Do hold list density at 36px desktop rows and 44px touch rows on the 4px scale, and cap scrollers to whole rows measured from the rendered row height.
Do keep panels flat (1px hairline, 10px radius) and reserve the shadow vocabulary for lifted overlays only.
Do draw the profile runs and the Route Trace once per mount (180 to 260ms linear) and snap them to final state under reduced motion.
Do put the plain name of every control and state in the interface, with metaphor display names beside plain truth.
Do let the trail-report strip report only what the API can prove: repo, out-of-sync issues, WIP counts, milestone target, task count.
donts: Don't use a state colour for decoration or an identity hue for state; ambiguous colour is a defect.
Don't let a ribbon carry colour alone, and don't fix ribbon tones to priority semantics: they follow each project's configured priority names in rank order.
Don't float anything but dialogs, slideovers, popovers, and dragged cards; no ambient shadows on rows, plates, panels, or resting buttons.
Don't invert the day map: never swap ribbons or plates, never use pure white ink, never turn the translation into a negative.
Don't animate ambiently: no loops or breathing effects beyond the loading skeleton pulse, no motion that survives a reduced-motion request.
Don't invent sync truth the API cannot prove: no relative sync timestamp, no Retry sync control, and no history series the data cannot back.
Don't stretch a meter fill past the ruled limit or imply capacity the counts do not support.
Don't cut a card or a row: repack in whole cells instead.
